title.value: Tilavonemab in early Alzheimer’s disease: results from a phase 2, randomized, double-blind study
title.quote: Tilavonemab in early Alzheimer’s disease: results from a phase 2, randomized, double-blind study

design.value: Phase 2, multiple-dose, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study conducted at 60 sites in 11 countries
design.quote: This was a phase 2, multiple-dose, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study (Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT02880956 ) conducted at 60 sites in 11 countries
design.location: Materials and methods, 'Study design and participants'

phase.quote: This phase 2 study evaluated the safety and efficacy of tilavonemab, an anti-tau monoclonal antibody, in patients with early Alzheimer’s disease.

n.quote: A total of 453 patients were randomized, of whom 337 were treated with tilavonemab (300 mg, n = 108; 1000 mg, n = 116; 2000 mg, n = 113) and 116 received placebo.

n_description.value: 453 randomized out of 1360 screened; the intent-to-treat dataset included all randomized patients who received at least one study drug dose
n_description.quote: Efficacy analyses were performed on the intent-to-treat (ITT) dataset, which included all randomized patients who received at least one study drug dose.

population.value: Adults aged 55–85 years meeting NIA-AA criteria for mild cognitive impairment or probable Alzheimer's disease, with a CDR global score of 0.5, MMSE 22–30, RBANS-Delayed Memory Index score of <=85, a positive amyloid PET scan and a Modified Hachinski Ischemic Scale score of <=4
population.quote: patients aged 55–85 years meeting clinical criteria for early Alzheimer’s disease with a Clinical Dementia Rating-Global Score of 0.5, a Mini-Mental State Examination score of 22 to 30
population.location: Abstract; Materials and methods, 'Study design and participants'

followup.value: 96-week double-blind treatment period, preceded by a 12-week screening period and followed by a 20-week follow-up after the last study drug administration
followup.quote: The study consisted of a 12-week screening period, 96-week double-blind treatment period, and a 20-week follow-up after administration of the last study drug.

intervention.value: Tilavonemab 300 mg, 1000 mg or 2000 mg administered by intravenous infusion every 4 weeks
intervention.quote: randomized 1:1:1:1 to receive one of three doses of tilavonemab (300 mg, 1000 mg, or 2000 mg) or placebo via intravenous infusion every 4 weeks

comparator.value: Placebo (n = 116) administered by intravenous infusion every 4 weeks
comparator.quote: in a 1:1:1:1 ratio to receive one of three tilavonemab doses (300 mg, 1000 mg, 2000 mg) or placebo administered via intravenous infusion every 4 weeks

biomarker_confirmation.value: A positive amyloid PET scan was required for entry (mean baseline amyloid PET 99.0 ± 31.1 centiloid); tau PET was not available at study start and was added later in a subset
biomarker_confirmation.quote: a Repeated Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status-Delayed Memory Index (RBANS-DMI) score of ≤85; a positive amyloid PET scan; a Modified Hachinski Ischemic Scale score of ≤4
biomarker_confirmation.location: Materials and methods, 'Study design and participants'

cohorts: Cohort 1 (within-trial pharmacokinetics, safety-monitoring and CSF target-engagement cohort named by this study)

outcomes.name: Change from baseline to Week 96 in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: The primary efficacy end point was the change from baseline to Week 96 in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes (CDR-SB) score.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Least squares mean change from baseline versus placebo at Week 96: 300 mg (n = 85) −0.07; 1000 mg (n = 91) −0.06; 2000 mg (n = 81) 0.16 CDR-SB points
outcomes.quote: The least squares mean change from baseline at Week 96 in the CDR-SB score with tilavonemab was not significantly different compared with placebo [300 mg ( n = 85): −0.07 (95% confidence interval, CI: −0.83 to 0.69);

outcomes.name: Secondary efficacy endpoints through Week 96, including global clinical impact and decline in patient cognition
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Secondary efficacy endpoints are listed in .
outcomes.quote: Similarly, through Week 96, there was no significant difference across treatment groups in any of the secondary outcomes assessed, including global clinical impact and decline in patient cognition ().

outcomes.name: Whole-brain, medial temporal lobe and lateral ventricle volume by volumetric MRI (vMRI)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: No treatment effect on whole-brain, medial temporal lobe or lateral ventricle volume (data not shown for the latter two)
outcomes.quote: Tilavonemab did not affect whole-brain volume over time (), nor was there any evidence of a treatment effect on medial temporal lobe or lateral ventricle volume as measured by vMRI (data not shown).

outcomes.name: Hippocampal volume by volumetric MRI (vMRI)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Week 28, tilavonemab 1000 mg versus placebo: −94.9 versus −121.6 mm3; Week 44, tilavonemab 2000 mg versus placebo: −127.9 versus −165.9 mm3; these were the only time points reaching statistical significance and no multiplicity adjustment was applied
outcomes.quote: Hippocampal volume was significantly less decreased at Week 28 in the tilavonemab 1000 mg group compared with placebo (−94.9 versus −121.6 mm 3 , respectively; P = 0.03)

outcomes.name: Plasma neurofilament light chain (NFL) and CSF NFL levels
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: No evidence of a treatment effect on plasma NFL or CSF NFL levels
outcomes.quote: Similarly, there was no evidence of a treatment effect on plasma NFL or CSF NFL levels (), nor was there evidence of a treatment effect in the amount of tau deposits in any Braak regions

outcomes.name: Tau PET standardized uptake value ratio (SUVR) in Braak regions I-VI
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: No evidence of a treatment effect on the amount of tau deposits in any Braak region, in the subset of patients with baseline and Week 96 scans (tau PET: n = 59 at baseline, n = 115 at Week 44, n = 128 at Week 96)
outcomes.quote: nor was there evidence of a treatment effect in the amount of tau deposits in any Braak regions based on the tau PET SUVR analyses that were completed in a subset of patients

outcomes.name: CSF free tau concentration at Week 12 (target engagement, not a clinical efficacy measure)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Patients in Cohort 1 underwent more frequent pharmacokinetics (PK) sampling, safety monitoring by the data monitoring committee, and target engagement assessment based on measurements of CSF free tau.
outcomes.effect_estimate: CSF free tau levels significantly lower than placebo at Week 12 in the 1000 mg and 2000 mg groups (Cohort 1)
outcomes.quote: Compared with placebo, CSF free tau levels were significantly lower at Week 12 in the tilavonemab 1000 mg ( P = 0.028) and tilavonemab 2000 mg ( P = 0.002) treatment groups ().

outcomes.name: CSF total tau concentration at Week 12
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Significantly lower than placebo in the 300 mg group only; not different from placebo in the higher-dose groups
outcomes.quote: CSF total tau concentrations were significantly lower in the tilavonemab 300 mg group ( P = 0.024 versus placebo) but were not different from placebo in the higher-dose groups ().

outcomes.name: Plasma total tau concentration
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: Exploratory outcomes assessed the effects of tilavonemab on potential markers of disease progression.
outcomes.effect_estimate: Plasma total tau levels significantly increased in all tilavonemab-treated patients compared with placebo
outcomes.quote: Plasma total tau levels were significantly increased in all treated patients compared with placebo ( P < 0.001 for all comparisons; ).
outcomes.location: Results, target engagement paragraph; Figure 3 caption

outcomes.name: Exposure-response analysis of tilavonemab exposure versus the primary and key secondary end points
outcomes.effect_estimate: No improvement in the primary or key secondary end points with increasing tilavonemab exposures
outcomes.quote: Preliminary exposure-response results showed no improvement in the primary or key secondary end points with increasing tilavonemab exposures ().

outcomes.name: ANCOVA subgroup analysis of CDR-SB mean score change from baseline by sex and by age (<65 years versus >=65 years)
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: An analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model was used for CDR-SB score subgroup analysis and CSF biomarkers for each scheduled visit.
outcomes.effect_estimate: A numerical differential effect in male versus female patients and in patients younger than 65 years versus 65 years and older; statistical significance was not achieved for any tilavonemab dose group after adjustment for multiple comparisons
outcomes.p_value: Treatment x Gender interaction P = 0.227; Treatment x Age group interaction P = 0.064
outcomes.quote: An ANCOVA subgroup analysis of CDR-SB mean score change from baseline revealed a numerical differential effect observed in male versus female patients and those aged younger than 65 years versus those aged 65 years and older ().

outcomes.name: CDR-SB subgroup analyses by ApoE4 carrier status, geographic location, baseline Alzheimer's disease medication use and baseline amyloid burden
outcomes.prespecification_evidence: An analysis of covariance (ANCOVA) model was used for CDR-SB score subgroup analysis and CSF biomarkers for each scheduled visit.
outcomes.effect_estimate: No differential treatment effect observed in any of these subgroups
outcomes.quote: No differential treatment effect was observed for subgroups based on ApoE4 carrier status, patients’ geographic location, baseline Alzheimer’s disease medication use, or baseline amyloid burden measured by PET ().

primary_endpoint_status.explanation: The primary endpoint, change from baseline to Week 96 in CDR-SB, was not met: no tilavonemab dose differed significantly from placebo (300 mg −0.07, 95% CI −0.83 to 0.69; 1000 mg −0.06, 95% CI −0.81 to 0.68; 2000 mg 0.16, 95% CI −0.60 to 0.93; all P ≥ 0.05), and CDR-SB worsened in every group.
primary_endpoint_status.quote: Tilavonemab was generally well tolerated but did not demonstrate efficacy in treating patients with early Alzheimer’s disease. Further investigations of tilavonemab in early Alzheimer’s disease are not warranted.

multiplicity.approach: Bonferroni method to adjust multiplicity, with one-sided testing at the 2.5% significance level, in the powering and testing framework for the primary CDR-SB endpoint; the exploratory hippocampal volume comparisons are explicitly described as being without multiplicity adjustment, and the age subgroup analysis was adjusted for multiple comparisons across the three dose groups
multiplicity.quote: using a one-sided test at the 2.5% significance level with Bonferroni method to adjust multiplicity

limitations: The natural history of the disease in the study population: patients clinically diagnosed with early Alzheimer's disease may already be too advanced pathologically to benefit from an anti-tau antibody
Tau imaging was not available when the trial began, so the effect of tilavonemab on tau accumulation could be assessed only in a small subset of patients
Lack of diversity in the study population, as most participants were White and well educated
Small sample size (15 to 28 patients per tilavonemab dose group) in the younger-than-65-years subgroup contributes to uncertainty about the observed treatment effect in that subgroup
The magnitude of decrease in CSF tau necessary for clinical benefit is unknown

risk_of_bias.judgement: The sponsor funded the trial and participated in design, research, collection, analysis and interpretation of the data, and most authors are AbbVie employees who may hold AbbVie stock.
risk_of_bias.quote: AbbVie Inc. funded the research for this study and participated in the study design; study research; and collection, analysis, and interpretation of the data.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The only positive imaging findings (hippocampal volume at Week 28 and Week 44) are nominal, at isolated time points, and explicitly without multiplicity adjustment.
risk_of_bias.quote: however, these were the only time points with statistical significance between groups without multiplicity adjustment ().

risk_of_bias.domain: interim analyses / data monitoring committee access to efficacy data
risk_of_bias.judgement: Three interim efficacy analyses were performed and the data monitoring committee reviewed unblinded efficacy data during the trial.
risk_of_bias.quote: Interim efficacy analyses were also performed when 8 patients/group, 35 patients/group, and 55 patients/group, respectively, completed the Week 96 visit.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Analysis of the primary endpoint at Week 96 rested on 85, 91 and 81 patients in the three tilavonemab groups out of 108, 116 and 113 randomized, with missing data handled by multiple imputation applied separately within treatment groups.
risk_of_bias.quote: Missing data were handled using multiple imputation applied separately for each treatment group.

risk_of_bias.judgement: The trial population was overwhelmingly White and well educated, which the document itself flags as a limitation.
risk_of_bias.quote: An additional limitation is the lack of diversity in the study population, as most of the participants were White and well educated.

risk_of_bias.judgement: Tau PET was added after the study commenced and only a subset of patients contributed scans, limiting the assessment of the drug's effect on tau accumulation.
risk_of_bias.quote: Tau PET imaging was initiated during the trial at a limited number of sites and was therefore assessed in a subset of patients

disagreements.question: Should tilavonemab be developed further in early Alzheimer's disease?
disagreements.position: This document concludes that further investigation of tilavonemab in early Alzheimer's disease is not warranted and that the data do not support it.
disagreements.quote: Overall, data from this phase 2 study do not support further investigations of tilavonemab for the treatment of early Alzheimer’s disease.

disagreements.question: Would higher doses of tilavonemab produce clinical benefit?
disagreements.position: This document argues higher doses are unlikely to help, because the CSF free tau reduction plateaus at higher exposures.
disagreements.attributed_to: Florian et al., citing the PSP study by Höglinger et al.
disagreements.quote: Therefore, it seems unlikely that higher doses of tilavonemab will show clinical benefit.

disagreements.question: Is the N-terminus of tau an appropriate antibody target?
disagreements.position: This document argues that antibodies directed against the N-terminus may be less effective than those targeting the mid-domain region.
disagreements.quote: This suggests that anti-tau antibodies directed against the N-terminus may be less effective than those that target the mid-domain region.

disagreements.question: Does target engagement imply clinical benefit?
disagreements.position: This document reports clear target engagement (reduced CSF free tau) alongside an absence of clinical efficacy, and treats the two as separate findings.
disagreements.quote: Despite lack of treatment efficacy, there was evidence of target engagement. The decrease of CSF free tau (i.e. tau not bound by antibodies) indicates that the doses assessed were sufficient to engage CSF tau.

disagreements.question: Are the negative results consistent with other N-terminal anti-tau antibody programmes?
disagreements.position: This document states its negative findings are consistent with gosuranemab and semorinemab, which also failed to slow disease progression while being well tolerated.
disagreements.attributed_to: Florian et al., citing trials of gosuranemab and semorinemab
disagreements.quote: In separate trials, gosuranemab and semorinemab, IgG4 monoclonal antibodies that target the N-terminal of extracellular tau, failed to slow disease progression in patients with mild cognitive impairment due to Alzheimer’s disease and mild Alzheimer’s disease but were well tolerated.
